info.title: Movie Night API
info.description:
API Gateway documentation for the Movie Night microservices platform.

NOTE: none of the downstream services (Movie-Service, Session-Service, Chat-Service) enforce authentication themselves — they trust an `X-User-ID` header on the request. `bearerAuth` below is documented at the gateway level assuming the Gateway validates the JWT and injects that header; this could not be confirmed from the provided code, since the Gateway itself isn't included.

ValidationErrorResponse.description: Default DRF validation error body. Shape varies by endpoint/field — shown as an open object because the code raises ValidationError with different keys in different views.

password.description: Validated by Django's validate_password (standard strength rules).

LoginRequest.description: LoginView uses TokenObtainPairSerializer as-is; email is the registration identifier per UserSerializer, consistent with it being the USERNAME_FIELD.

ProfileUpdateRequest.description: Only `display_name` and `password` are writable here (email/id/created_at/updated_at are read_only on UpdateProfileSerializer). `display_name` is required by ProfileView.perform_update.

password.description: Optional. NOTE: unlike UserSerializer, UpdateProfileSerializer does not mark this write_only, so the stored password value is also included in the 200 response body below (see ProfileUpdateResponse) — appears to be an oversight in the code, documented as-is.

WatchHistoryRequest.description: NOTE: the view does not actually validate `rating` (no min/max check, no required check at the view level — it is passed straight to `Watched.objects.get_or_create` as `defaults={'rating': request.data.get('rating')}`). Constraints below reflect the field's declared shape only, not enforced behavior confirmed in code.

answer.description: Must match one of the option strings for the session's current question (validated against `current_question['options']`).
answer.example: I want something funny and light.

WrappedResponse.description: Inferred wrapper shape used by common.response.success_response(data=..., message=..., status=...). The helper's implementation was not provided, so this is an assumption, not a confirmed shape.

ProfileUpdateResponse.description: Same as UserProfile, but also includes `password` (the hashed value) since UpdateProfileSerializer doesn't set write_only on it. Likely unintentional, documented as the code actually behaves.

Movie.description: Full movie details, returned by GET /api/movies/{movie_id}.

user_id.description: Stored as-is from the X-User-ID header; not necessarily numeric.

Session.description: Movie Night collaborative session. Fields shown are confirmed or strongly implied; `additionalProperties` covers the rest of `fields = "__all__"` since the Session model wasn't provided.

question.description: Present when completed=false. Shape comes from the QUESTIONS list, which is not in the provided code.
Shape comes from QUESTIONS[0], which is not in the provided code.

recommendation.description: Raw output of LLMService.recommend_movie(); known to contain at least 'movie_title' since the view reads recommendation['movie_title']. Full shape unverified (LLMService not provided).

movie.description: Output of MovieService.get_movie_details(); not provided in code.

message.example: Could not find the recommended movie.

post.description: Create a new user account. Subject to RegisterThrottle (no explicit 429 documented — throttle response body/behavior not shown in the provided code).

201.description: User created successfully. `data` holds the serialized user (UserProfile shape, via UserSerializer).

post.description: Authenticate a user and return JWT tokens. Subject to LoginThrottle.
Generate a new access token using a valid refresh token.

401.description: Invalid or expired refresh token (raised as InvalidToken).

post.description: Log out the currently authenticated user by blacklisting their refresh token.

400.description: Refresh token missing from the request body.

patch.description: NOTE: only `display_name` is actively validated by ProfileView.perform_update. If `display_name` is provided but unchanged from the current value, the view's own 400 branch (`return Response(...)` inside perform_update) is never actually sent to the client — DRF's default update() ignores perform_update's return value and still responds 200 with the serializer data (unsaved).

200.description: Movie search results. Raw pass-through of MovieService.search_movie(); exact shape not in provided code.

400.description: Query is missing, or no movies were found for the given query.

get.description:
Returns the locally cached Movie if it exists; otherwise fetches it from TMDBService, persists it, and returns it.

NOTE: there is no explicit 404 handling in MovieDetailView — if the TMDB call fails to find the movie, the resulting exception is not caught in the provided code, so it would surface as an unhandled server error rather than a clean 404.

200.description: Recommended movies. Raw pass-through of MovieService.get_movie_recommendations(); exact shape not in provided code.

400.description: No movies found for this ID.

get.description: NOTE: WatchlistView declares DjangoFilterBackend but `filterset_fields` is commented out in the provided code, so no query-parameter filtering is actually active on this endpoint.

post.description: Add the specified movie to the current user's watchlist. `movie_id` here is the Movie's own ID (Movie.objects.filter(id=...)).

400.description: Movie not found, or already in the user's watchlist.

delete.description: NOTE: unlike POST, this endpoint filters `Watchlist.objects.filter(id=movie_id, ...)` — i.e. `movie_id` here actually refers to the Watchlist row's own primary key, not the movie's ID. This is an inconsistency in the code, not a documentation choice.

parameters.name: movie_id
parameters.description: Watchlist entry ID (not the movie's ID — see description).

400.description: Movie is not in the watchlist.

parameters.name: rating
parameters.description: Filter watched movies by rating. (This one IS active — WatchedHistoryView declares filterset_fields = ['rating'].)

post.description:
Mark a movie as watched with an optional rating.

NOTE: as a side effect, this also deletes any matching Watchlist entry for the same movie/user — not documented anywhere else in the API surface, but it is real behavior in WatchedEditView.post.

requestBody.description: Optional rating for the watched movie.

400.description: Movie not found, or already marked as watched by this user.

delete.description: NOTE: this appears to be a bug in the provided code — WatchedEditView.delete actually queries the Watchlist model (`Watchlist.objects.filter(id=movie_id, user_id=user_id)`), not Watched. So calling this endpoint deletes a Watchlist row (by its own ID, same caveat as the watchlist DELETE endpoint), not a Watched row, despite the success message saying 'removed from watched history'. Documented here as the code actually behaves.

parameters.name: movie_id
parameters.description: Watchlist entry ID (see description — this endpoint queries Watchlist, not Watched).

200.description: Row removed (see description for the Watchlist/Watched mismatch).

post.description: Create a new collaborative movie session. The authenticated user (via X-User-ID) becomes the leader.
Join an existing session using its 6-digit session code.

400.description: Invalid code, session not joinable (not waiting), or already a member.

get.description: Only returns sessions the current user participates in (queryset filtered by participants__user_id).

404.description: Session not found, or the user is not a participant.

post.description: Start the session. Requires: the caller is a leader-role participant, at least 2 members, the session is currently WAITING, and at least one participant has a non-empty watchlist.

400.description: Session not found, caller is not a member, caller is not the leader, fewer than 2 members, session already started, or no participant has any movies in their watchlist.

post.description: End the session and record the selected movie. Requires: the caller is a leader-role participant and the session is currently ACTIVE.

requestBody.description: ID of the movie the group selected.

400.description: Session not found, caller is not a member, caller is not the leader, session is not active, or movie_tmdb_id missing.

post.description: Start a conversational AI movie recommendation session.
Submit an answer to the current AI recommendation question.

requestBody.description: Answer to the current recommendation question.

400.description: No active recommendation session for this id/user, answer missing, or answer not one of the current question's options.

post.description: Complete the recommendation conversation, ask the LLM for a movie title, then look it up via the Movie Service.

400.description: No active recommendation session for this id/user, or not all questions have been answered yet.

404.description: The movie title recommended by the LLM could not be found via TMDB search.

503.description: LLM call or movie lookup failed (caught generic exception).
